title: onboarding-briefcase-mini-course-and-prompt-blackbox
summary: A compact, reusable 30-60 minute onboarding 'briefcase' for new integrators and early adopters that bundles a one-click demo, curated prompt pack (the 'blackbox'), pairing scripts, and lightweight eval hooks for prompt quality checks.
audience: New engineers integrating Redwood in small proof-of-concept projects; solutions engineers running 1:1 onboarding sessions; docs writers who will derive quickstarts and sample prompts.
goals: Get a developer from zero to a reproducible demo in 30 minutes (local or hosted)
Provide a set of curated prompts (blackbox) that demonstrate best-practice usage and failure modes
Surface telemetry points and simple eval hooks so adopters can measure prompt drift/regressions early
Create modular artifacts that can be embedded in workshops, PRDs, and support playbooks
modules: 0 - Briefcase overview (2 min): what this kit contains and when to use it
1 - Install & credential shortcut (5 min): one-liners for npm/pip + env var helper + redwood token guide
2 - One-click demo runner (10 min): local server + sample UI using the briefcase manifest
3 - Prompt Blackbox (10-15 min): 8 curated prompts, annotated expected outputs, known brittleness notes
4 - Pairing scripts (5-10 min): facilitator scripts for 1:1 walkthroughs and customer demos
5 - Eval hooks & telemetry (5 min): small test harness, prompt checks, and telemetry knobs to enable in dev projects
6 - Handoff checklist & next steps (2 min): integration checklist, security pointers, and escalation contacts
telemetry: Minimal required telemetry: request_id, model_name, prompt_hash, user_flow_tag, latency_ms, response_token_count, confidence_hint (heuristic). Provide a 1-file test harness (node/python) that posts curated prompts and records baseline outputs for regression detection.
metrics: demo-repeatability: number of unchanged outputs for stable prompts
open_questions: Should the briefcase auto-bootstrap a local Redis for caching or rely on an in-memory stub?
What subset of telemetry fields are allowed in the short-form privacy-safe example for public docs?
Do we ship the blackbox as a separate file in the repo or bake into the quickstart CLI?
Ownership: who triages incoming reports when curated prompts show unexpected drift? (SEs or Research?)
next_steps: Prototype the one-click demo runner in a tiny repo: target 1 day prototype (RW-1827)
Lock 8 initial prompts and write annotation notes (owner: Priya) - 3 days
Build the telemetry test harness and baseline runbook (owner: Diego) - 5 days
Run 3 internal pairing sessions and capture facilitator feedback (owner: Maya) - 1 week
Convert the briefcase into a minimal GitHub template and link into product quickstarts
body:
Context
This doc is an authoring draft for a very small, portable onboarding kit (the "briefcase"). We want something that an SE or engineer can drop into a customer's machine or into a workshop VM and run with minimal friction. The emphasis is on reproducibility, signal for regressions, and a small set of well-annotated prompts that teach good prompt design and reveal typical failure modes.

Why another quickstart?
We already have longer quickstarts and monolithic labs, but adoption conversations often need a compact, trustworthy artifact that: (a) runs fast, (b) demonstrates observability hooks, and (c) gives clear guidance on prompt tradeoffs. The briefcase is intentionally opinionated: it shows one recommended flow rather than many choices.

Design principles
- Minimal surface area: one command to run the demo, one file to edit.
- Telemetry-first: include evaluative checks baked into the demo so regressions are caught early.
- Annotated prompts: each prompt includes expected shape, guards, and deprecation notes.
- Reusable artifacts: should be easily embedded into workshops and internal SE runbooks.

Quick content sketch
- repo/manifest: briefcase.json (manifest with demo assets)
- scripts/: start-demo.sh, run-evals.py
- prompts/: blackbox-prompts.csv (id, prompt, expected_snippet, brittleness_notes)
- docs/: facilitator.md, handoff-checklist.md

Facilitator hints (short)
- Start by explaining the goal: reproducible demo that surfaces observability.
- Run the 3 canonical prompts first (happy path, edge case, adversarial input) and show difference in outputs and telemetry.
- Use pairing script to ask the integrator to tweak one prompt and observe effect on output and latency.

Failure modes to call out
- Non-deterministic outputs: show baseline vs. live and explain how to pin sampling/temperature.
- Token budget surprise: demonstrate token_count telemetry and how to change prompt compression.
- Hidden assumptions: identify system messages or user context that change outputs.

Appendix: small sketch of blackbox prompt entries
1. Summarize: "Summarize the following user message in 2 lines." (expected: concise summary; brittle if user message contains code blocks)
2. Extract entities: "Return name, email, and action as JSON." (expected: JSON object; brittle if input mixes languages)
3. Rephrase for tone: "Rephrase to be friendly and 3rd-person." (expected: changed tone; watch for hallucinated facts)

Notes to self
- Keep this doc short; move large examples to the repo.
- Coordinate with docs team to produce a privacy-safe public variant that strips telemetry but keeps the demo runner.
- Schedule a sync with Research to define prompt ownership and regression triage flow.
